subject: Request: short-term log/backup retention carveout for Acme Health audit
messages:
From: J. Peters <j.peters@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary extension for backup/log retention for upcoming audit

Hi Soojin,

We're kicking off an external compliance assessment next week and need a short-lived retention exception for a subset of our logs and backups stored with Redwood. Specifically:

- Backup snapshots for the period 2026-11-01 through 2026-12-31 (retain for 180 days instead of standard 90)
- Application request logs (index & debug) for the same period, kept for 120 days instead of 30

This is strictly for audit evidence; Acme will purge everything after Nov 30, 2027. Can Redwood provide a documented carveout and an amendment to the DPA (or an SOW addendum) that shows the adjusted retention windows and subprocessor scope? We also need confirmation whether backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys or Redwood-managed keys, and whether a KMS-scoped exception is required.

Attached is our evidence request spreadsheet to help map the assets (acme-evidence-request.xlsx). We'd like to lock this down by March 25 to meet auditor timelines. Please advise next steps and if you need any more info.

Thanks,
J. Peters
Director, Compliance
Acme Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: J. Peters <j.peters@acmehealth.com>, Legal Ops <legal-ops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension for backup/log retention for upcoming audit

Thanks Jason — appreciate the timeline and the spreadsheet. I've looped in Legal (Kimberly) and Engineering (Marcus) to scope feasibility and the DPA amendment needs. Quick answers up-front:

- We can support a temporary extension scoped to the specific snapshot ranges you listed; engineering needs to confirm the exact purge window and whether a manual hold is required.
- Backups are encrypted at rest; for your account they are Redwood-managed KMS by default. We offer a customer-managed KMS option on Dedicated/Private, but for Hosted accounts we can discuss an exception or temporary key escrow for the evidence window.

Actions I propose:
1) Marcus: confirm how long we need to hold the snapshots before automatic purge, and whether we can apply a label-based retention hold.
2) Kimberly: advise on language for a short-term DPA amendment or SOW addendum that documents 180/120-day retention for these specific assets and a one-time extension until 2027-11-30.
3) Mateo/Vivek: cost and billing impact (if any) and whether we need a signed DocuSign amendment.

I'll compile and send a single formal response + proposed amendment draft by EOD Friday (Mar 12).

— Soojin
Sr. Product Manager, Privacy & Controls
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, J. Peters <j.peters@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension for backup/log retention for upcoming audit

On Thu, Mar 11, 2027 at 10:05 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Jason — appreciate the timeline and the spreadsheet. I've looped in Legal (Kimberly) and Engineering (Marcus) to scope feasibility and the DPA amendment needs.

Quick tech summary from infra:
- We can apply label-scoped retention holds to backup snapshots; that will prevent automatic purge and is reversible.
- For hosted accounts, snapshots use Redwood KMS keys (AES-256) in our managed key ring. We can put a temporary export/escrow in place for evidence retrieval, but we do not rotate to a customer-managed KMS without a Dedicated/Private contract.
- Proposed implementation: tag the relevant snapshots with an "acme-audit-2027" hold; set retention policy of 180d for those snapshots and 120d for the identified logs. The purge job will skip tagged snapshots until the hold is removed.

Operational notes:
- We will need an explicit signed instruction from Acme (DocuSign ok) to apply the hold; ops will log the change and provide a signed audit record.
- We estimate no more than a single-day operational lift to apply tags and configure the retention exception; retrieval of the sample logs (attached) is straightforward.

Attachment: logs-sample-2026-12-01.tar.gz (sanitized) — sample format and size.

I'll coordinate with ops for exact timestamps once legal signs off.

— Marcus
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, J. Peters <j.peters@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension for backup/log retention for upcoming audit

Thanks for the details. I reviewed the spreadsheet and Marcus's notes. From a contracting perspective we can do a limited-scope amendment to the DPA that: 

- Identifies specific assets (by snapshot id range and S3 key prefixes) to be held beyond standard retention;
- Defines the temporary retention values (snapshots: 180 days; logs: 120 days) and a final purge date of 2027-11-30 unless otherwise extended by mutual written consent;
- States that the exception is solely for audit/evidence purposes and that Acme will bear any marginal storage costs for the extended retention period;
- Requires Acme to provide a signed instruction (DocuSign) authorizing the hold and listing the snapshot IDs/prefixes.

Two points for discussion:
1) KMS scope: since this is a hosted account with Redwood-managed keys, we will document that backups are encrypted with Redwood-managed KMS and include a statement that no keys will be exported beyond what is necessary for evidence retrieval. If Acme requires customer-managed keys for the evidence window, we will need a dedicated/private deployment; that is out-of-scope for a short amendment.
2) Subprocessors: we should list any subprocessor that will have access to the held assets for the audit (ops, SRE, and our storage partner). Please confirm whether Acme needs an updated subprocessor list included in the amendment.

I've attached a draft amendment (proposed-retention-amendment-draft.pdf) — review and comment. If acceptable, I can ready it for signature and route via DocuSign.

— Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Legal
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: J. Peters <j.peters@acmehealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Legal Ops <legal-ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary extension for backup/log retention for upcoming audit

Folks — wrapping up on this thread. Summary and agreed next steps: 

1) Scope: snapshots 2026-11-01 -> 2026-12-31 and request/diagnostic logs with prefix acme/requests/* will be held (tagged) and retained per the amendment (snapshots 180d; logs 120d).
2) KMS: Hosted account uses Redwood-managed KMS; we will not rotate to customer-managed KMS. We will provide an evidence export process and signed audit logs; no key export will occur.
3) Subprocessors: we will include StoragePartner Co. and our Ops/SRE teams in the subprocessor paragraph of the amendment. Confirm if Acme wants to CC any procurement contacts for the subprocessor listing.
4) Cost: Mateo to follow up with a one-time estimated storage delta; Acme will cover marginal costs for the extension.
5) Approvals & signature: Kimberly will finalize the DPA addendum and post it to the Drive folder; Acme to approve and sign via DocuSign by Mar 25. Link: https://www.docusign.net/abcdef-ACME-retention-amend

Kimberly, Marcus, Mateo — please confirm you are good with the summary and I will send the final package to Acme and ops for scheduling the hold.

Thanks everyone — Soojin
Sr. Product Manager, Privacy & Controls
Redwood Inference
